answer: Each agent carries a cryptographic reputation token tinted like pigment on an umber canvas; its weight grows only when the token is repeatedly referenced by distinct, long‑standing agents that have themselves accrued reputation through verified work. When a new identity appears, its token is assigned a quadratic penalty so that a swarm of wander‑ing clones adds up to less than a single mature token, forcing the attacker to invest linearly growing stake for each useful vote. The cost rises quadratically with the number of fake IDs, making sybil floods economically infeasible.
